name: Desktop Agent
author: Zedster07
description: Speak to your desktop and have it act, on a leash you own. Adds spoken commands on top of Omarchy's built-in Voxtype dictation: a phrase is matched against a declared intent registry, gated by a default-deny policy with an approval overlay and an audit trail. Other plugins can register their own voice commands.

barWidget.description: Spoken commands, an approval overlay, and policy-gated agent control.

schema.label: Spoken commands
schema.description: Match a spoken phrase against the intent registry and run it, instead of typing it. Dictation is unaffected either way — that is Voxtype's job and this never touches it.

schema.label: Confirm spoken commands
schema.description: Whether a matched command raises the approval overlay before running. Intents marked destructive always ask, whatever this says.

schema.label: Let other plugins register commands
schema.description: Read voice-intents.json from other installed plugins so their actions can be spoken. Each plugin has to be approved once before its intents go live — installing a plugin must not silently extend what your microphone can do.

schema.label: Match strictness (%)
schema.description: How close a phrase must be to a registered command before it runs. Higher means more phrases are rejected as unrecognised, which is the safe direction: an unmatched command says so, a wrongly matched one just happens.

schema.label: AI assistance
schema.description: off: only phrases in the command list work. route: when nothing matches, a LOCAL model picks from the same list — it can recognise a new wording but cannot invent an action, and nothing leaves the machine. route+plan: also lets your AI CLI write a new command for requests the list does not cover, such as playing something on YouTube. Planned commands are checked against a denylist and always need your approval.

schema.label: AI provider
schema.description: auto uses a local Ollama model for recognising wordings and your installed CLI agent for planning new commands. Only providers found on this machine are used.

schema.label: Local model
schema.description: Ollama model used for recognising wordings. Small and fast matters more than clever here — it is choosing from a list of about a dozen.

schema.label: Agent control (MCP)
schema.description: Allow an MCP client such as Claude Code to drive the desktop through the same policy. Voice works with this off.

schema.label: End-of-run recap
schema.description: After the agent has been idle a while, slide in a card listing everything it did. Never takes focus.

schema.label: Recap idle window (seconds)
schema.description: MCP has no end-of-task signal, so a run counts as finished once the desktop has been quiet this long.

schema.label: Maximum unattended lease (minutes)
schema.description: Hard ceiling on a full-access lease, re-checked on every action. A longer lease is truncated, not honoured.
